Literally Me
LIT-er-uh-lee MEE
phrase (Gen Alpha slang)
From a 2022–23 meme in which young men posted images of brooding, lonely, often violent film characters — Ryan Gosling’s driver in Drive (2011) and K in Blade Runner 2049 (2017), the Joker (2019), Patrick Bateman, Travis Bickle of Taxi Driver (1976) — with the caption "literally me." The "literally me" characters became a recognized list. Gen Alpha uses the phrase more broadly and lightly — "this sleepy cat is literally me" — but the brooding-hero sense lives on in edits.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

"Literally me" means "that’s exactly like me" — said about a character, an animal video, or a meme. Gen Alpha kids say it about anything relatable, and older boys say it about a set of lonely, angry movie men. The Christian observation: the phrase is about identification — who do I see myself in? — and that is one of the most important questions a child ever answers. Scripture says a believer is being shaped into one image above all: God’s people are "predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son" (Rom 8:29). Paul could say, "Be ye followers of me, even as I also am of Christ" (1Co 11:1), because he was looking at Jesus. The "literally me" heroes are mostly men who are lonely, bitter, and violent, and the Psalm warns about walking in their counsel: "Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners" (Psa 1:1). Whom a boy calls "literally me" he is likely to become. The better answer is "looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith" (Heb 12:2). A father can tell a five-year-old: "It’s fun when a cartoon is just like us! But the best one to be like is Jesus — and God is making us more like Him every day."

Webster 1828 Definition

Meme caption (2022–23) identifying with brooding film men, now any relatable thing — a question of identification, answered by the image of the Son into which believers are conformed.

LITERALLY ME, phr. (internet meme, 2022–present; Gen Alpha usage) "That is exactly like me"; said of a character, image, or video. "This hamster stuffing his face is literally me."

Meme canon: the "literally me" characters — Gosling’s driver and K, the Joker, Patrick Bateman, Travis Bickle, Tyler Durden.

Decode for parents: light in a child’s mouth, heavier in a teen’s; notice which characters.

Key Scripture

Rom 8:29 — "For whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brethren."

1Co 11:1 — "Be ye followers of me, even as I also am of Christ."

Psa 1:1 — "Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful."

Heb 12:2 — "Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God."

Modern Corruption

"Literally me" teaches young men to find themselves in lonely, bitter, violent heroes; Scripture says the believer is being conformed to the image of Christ and calls him to look unto Jesus.

expand to see more

Identification is formation. The "literally me" canon is a gallery of isolated, wounded, often murderous men, presented with sympathy and style. A teenage boy who sees himself in them is being offered a story about his loneliness: that it makes him special, that his anger is justified, that he is the misunderstood hero. That story has ended badly in real life.

Give your son better mirrors. Tell him the stories of David, Daniel, Nehemiah, and above all Christ, and of real men you know who are faithful. Ask him who he thinks is "literally him" and listen. Then tell him the truth Rom 8:29 holds out: God intends him to look like Jesus.
